# Sensing Networks for Civic Resilience — synthetic proposal excerpt

FABRICATED FIXTURE (#22 rule: no real applicant material, ever). The applicant,
the institute, and the proposal are invented. The *cited literature* is a
deliberate mix, because that is what the checks are for:

- ref [1] cites a real paper with its real DOI and correct metadata
- ref [2] cites a plausible-looking journal article whose DOI is unregistered
- ref [3] attaches a real DOI to a title and author that are not that paper's
- ref [4] cites a host that cannot resolve at all
- ref [5] cites a page that resolves to "no such document"
- ref [6] carries an ISBN whose checksum does not hold
- ref [7] carries a DOI that is not DOI-shaped

## Background

Nanoscale sensing has reached the point where temperature can be measured
inside a living cell [1], and the same instrumentation is now proposed for
distributed civic monitoring [3]. Work on information environments suggests
that synthetic narratives outpace their corrections [2]. Our own prior review
of the field is available online [4], as is the program's technical note [5].
The framing follows the resilience literature [6] and its measurement
critique [7].
